_comment: R34 prototype geography; belongs in the pack later. Extents are interpretive placement envelopes, never surveyed 1861 boundaries or modern land cover. [I] means interpretation; all sources read 2026-11-18.

features.name: Wilderness of Spotsylvania
features.extentCertainty: medium for the named tract, low for exact boundary; roughly seventy square miles in the source. This is a symbolic placement envelope around the historical east-west road corridor, not a boundary survey.
features.existence1861: high; historian Michael P. Gray describes prewar second growth after iron works closed in the 1840s, before Catharine Furnace reopened at the start of the war

sources.basis: Michael P. Gray, Virginia Humanities; prewar woodland history and seventy-square-mile tract. Text facts only; no article images used.

features.interpretation: [I] Clumps indicate the named woodland, never comprehensive tree cover or a surveyed limit.

features.name: Great Dismal Swamp
features.extentCertainty: low; a conservative symbolic envelope near Lake Drummond, not the historical million-acre limit
features.existence1861: high; FWS describes drainage from 1763 and freedom-seeking communities through the Civil War

sources.basis: historical wetland in southeastern Virginia and northeastern North Carolina; over a million acres originally
1862 Coast Survey geographic reference; approximate placement only

features.interpretation: [I] Scattered tufts represent the named swamp only; the envelope is not a measured shoreline.

features.name: Okefenokee Swamp
features.extentCertainty: low; symbolic envelope in southeastern Georgia, not the modern refuge boundary
features.existence1861: high; FWS describes centuries of wetland continuity and the 1891 drainage attempt

sources.basis: Millennia-old peatland; 1891 Suwannee Canal Company purchase, relatively intact over centuries; Suwannee and St Marys headwaters

features.interpretation: [I] Modern refuge acreage is not asserted as an 1861 extent.
